models.name: GPT Image
tips: Write in full sentences — it reads prompts like a brief, not a tag list.
Put exact text you want rendered in quotes: a sign that says "OPEN".
State aspect ratio in words ("4:5 vertical", "wide 16:9").
Iterate conversationally: "same shot, warmer light, lower camera".

models.name: Nano Banana (Gemini Image)
tips: Describe the scene as a story; it rewards narrative detail over keyword lists.
Great at editing: upload a photo and say exactly what to change and what to keep.
For consistent characters, reuse the same reference image and name the character.
Ask for photographic terms explicitly — lens, aperture, time of day.

models.name: Midjourney
tips: Front-load the subject; later words carry less weight.
Parameters go at the end: --ar 3:2 --stylize 250 --chaos 10.
--sref copies a style from an image or code; --cref keeps a character.
Use --no instead of writing "without" in the prompt.

models.name: FLUX
tips: Long, plain-English descriptions work best — think art director notes.
Strong at text in images; quote it and say where it sits.
No negative prompt in most setups — describe what you want instead.
Layer the description: subject → setting → light → camera → finish.

models.name: Stable Diffusion / SDXL
tips: Comma-separated tags; weight with (word:1.3) to emphasise.
A negative prompt does real work here — list artefacts to avoid.
Checkpoints and LoRAs change everything; note which one you used.
Keep CFG around 5–7; higher makes images harsh.

models.name: Ideogram
tips: Best-in-class for typography — posters, logos, packaging.
Quote the exact words and describe the lettering style.
Pick a style preset (Design, Realistic, 3D) before tuning words.
Use Magic Prompt to expand a short idea, then edit what it wrote.

models.name: Imagen
tips: Clear photographic language: "close-up", "35mm", "golden hour".
Specify the medium early — photo, watercolour, 3D render.
Shorter prompts can work; add detail only where results drift.
Good at realistic hands and text; still check fine detail.

prompts.title: Ceramicist in her studio
prompts.subject: Portrait
segments: of an elderly ceramicist in her sunlit studio, hands dusted with clay, holding a half-finished vase.
soft window light from the left,
prompts.why: Naming a real lens and aperture gets you a believable portrait background blur; the magazine reference sets the whole colour grade in two words.

prompts.title: Floating headphones
prompts.subject: Product
segments: of matte sage-green wireless headphones floating above a smooth travertine plinth,
with a gentle gradient backdrop from cream to pale olive,
prompts.why: Materials ("matte", "travertine") do more than adjectives like "beautiful". The backdrop colours are chosen to echo the product so it reads as one palette.

prompts.title: City inside a tide pool
prompts.subject: 3D & miniature
segments: of a tiny coastal city built inside a tide pool, starfish bridges, barnacle houses, sea anemone trees,
prompts.why: Give the model concrete swaps (starfish → bridges) rather than "whimsical"; it builds the world from your nouns. Tilt-shift sells the miniature scale.

prompts.title: Tonkotsu ramen, top-down
prompts.subject: Food
segments: of a steaming bowl of tonkotsu ramen on a dark walnut table, chashu, soft-boiled egg, scallions, nori, chopsticks resting on the rim,
prompts.why: Listing the toppings means each one actually shows up. "Overhead flat-lay" fixes the camera angle so you don't get a random three-quarter view.

prompts.title: Shrine in a cedar forest
prompts.subject: Landscape
segments: of a moss-covered stone shrine deep in a misty cedar forest at dawn,
a small fox statue at the entrance,
prompts.why: One small focal detail (the fox statue) gives a big environment a place for the eye to land. Two-colour palettes keep painterly images from going muddy.

prompts.title: Teapot robot character sheet
prompts.subject: Character
segments: for a friendly robot mascot shaped like a teapot,
flat vector illustration, thick clean outlines,
limited palette of teal, coral and cream,
prompts.why: "Character sheet" plus naming the views gets a turnaround in one image — useful as a reference for later prompts or 3D modelling.

prompts.title: Brutalist library skylight
prompts.subject: Architecture
segments: of a brutalist concrete library interior with a massive circular skylight, people reading on tiered wooden steps,
afternoon sun casting a sharp circle of light,
prompts.why: Describing what the light does ("a sharp circle") beats naming the light source. People in the scene give the space a sense of scale.

prompts.title: Risograph cycling poster
prompts.subject: Poster & type
segments: of a cyclist riding through rolling hills,
two-color print in fluorescent pink and blue,
bold simple shapes, mid-century travel poster composition,
prompts.why: Print-process words (grain, misregistration) are what make it look printed rather than digital. "No text" stops the model inventing fake lettering.

prompts.title: Perfume bottle in a desert
prompts.subject: Product
segments: a faceted amber perfume bottle half-buried in rippled dunes,
prompts.why: Midjourney weights the start of the prompt most, so the subject leads. Unwanted things go in --no rather than in the sentence.

prompts.title: Rainy neon alley, anime still
prompts.subject: Illustration
segments: a girl with a clear umbrella waiting at a tiny ramen stall in a narrow rainy alley,
prompts.why: --niji switches to the anime-tuned model. A very wide ratio reads as a film frame on its own.

prompts.title: Coffee bag with real typography
prompts.subject: Poster & type
segments: A kraft-paper coffee bag standing on a marble counter.
The front label reads "NORTHBOUND ROASTERS" in a condensed serif, with "Ethiopia · Washed · 250g" in small caps underneath.
Morning light from a window on the right, soft shadows.
Shot like a Kinfolk product page, 50mm, f/4.
prompts.why: FLUX renders type well when you quote the exact words and describe the lettering. Plain sentences beat comma tags for this model.

prompts.title: Weathered knight portrait
prompts.subject: Character
segments: portrait of a weathered knight, scarred face, dented plate armour, (rain-soaked hair:1.2),
negative: blurry, lowres, extra fingers, deformed hands, watermark, text, oversaturated
prompts.why: Weighting with (term:1.2) nudges one detail without rewriting. The negative prompt is doing real work in SD — list the failure modes you keep seeing.

prompts.title: Bakery logo lockup
prompts.subject: Poster & type
segments: A logo for a neighbourhood bakery called "Rise & Crumb",
hand-lettered script wordmark above a simple wheat-stalk icon,
two colours: deep brown on cream,
flat vector, centred, plenty of margin
prompts.why: Ideogram's strength is lettering — quote the name and describe the type style. Limiting colours keeps it usable as a real logo.

prompts.title: Restyle a room photo
prompts.subject: Architecture
segments: Using the attached photo of my living room,
keep the walls, windows and floor exactly as they are.
Replace the furniture with a mid-century modern set in walnut and mustard fabric,
add a large fiddle-leaf fig by the window,
prompts.why: For edits, say what must not change before what should. Locking the camera angle stops the model re-framing the whole room.

prompts.title: Hiker above the clouds
prompts.subject: Landscape
segments: a lone hiker in a red jacket on a ridge above a sea of clouds,
prompts.why: A single strong colour (the red jacket) against a soft scene creates the focal point. Deep focus keeps both hiker and horizon sharp.
